hypothesis: Weather foundation models such as Aurora and Pangu-Weather, trained on diverse reanalysis and multi-source datasets, can produce high-resolution probabilistic atmospheric forecasts that are directly actionable for renewable energy grid scheduling and dispatch optimization. By coupling the sub-seasonal-to-seasonal predictive skill of these models with ML-driven power system optimization, grid operators could reduce curtailment of variable renewable generation and lower reserve margins required for balancing. This integration could unlock a new paradigm of "forecast-native" renewable energy planning, where the uncertainty quantification inherent in ensemble weather foundation models is propagated end-to-end into unit commitment and optimal power flow solvers, fundamentally changing how capacity adequacy is assessed.

The novel claim extrapolates that closing the loop—feeding ensemble uncertainty from weather foundation models directly into power system optimization—would constitute a qualitatively new planning paradigm not yet described in any retrieved source. Three additional relevant works not in the retrieved set that support components of this hypothesis are: (1) Lam et al., "GraphCast: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting," Science 382, 2023; (2) Nguyen et al., "ClimaX: A foundation model for weather and climate," ICML 2023 (arXiv:2301.10343); and (3) Morales et al., "Electricity market clearing with improved dispatch of stochastic production," European Journal of Operational Research, 2014—which together span foundation-model forecasting skill and stochastic dispatch under uncertainty.
